reader.requirement: At 85, after an unsuccessful I-O operation on a relative file, the file-name declarative runs (a), else the declarative of the file's open mode INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND, including a file in the process of being opened (b-e), except files named in a file-name USE, and none runs when the statement's AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence.

nothing: the file-name tier then open-mode tier are documented edition-invariant (kb/Work PB344)

reader.notes: __IoCheck returns before the tiers when the statement's AT END / INVALID KEY phrase covers the status family, then file-name tier, then FileOpenModeOf(__f) tier; the mode is set during OPEN so a failed OPEN selects its mode's declarative. All nine probe lines match the rule.

refuter.evidence: modes.cob (runs/modes-003) upholds the mode tiers: failed OPEN I-O -> D-IO 35, failed OPEN EXTEND -> D-EXT 35; READ after failed OPEN 47, WRITE not open 48, CLOSE not open 42, READ after CLOSE 47 -> no declarative (file in no mode); READ on OUTPUT file -> D-OUT 47; WRITE on INPUT file with INVALID KEY phrase -> D-IN 48 (phrase does not cover 48); OPEN INPUT while open -> D-IN 41; DELETE missing with INVALID KEY -> phrase only; DELETE / REWRITE (NOT INVALID KEY only) missing -> D-IO 23. But GR5b's exception fails on the GLOBAL path: nest3.cob (nest3-001, 85) N3 runs OUTER's GLOBAL INPUT declarative for FG, which OUTERP references by file-name-1 in another USE (same at 2023, nest3x). cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR5 the text is in GR5; OK §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR5b the text is in GR5b; OK §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1.
refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (wrong-answer, cause b), the same defect as 1985-GR-VIII.4.8.4-4: GR5b's 'except those files referenced by file-name-1 in another USE statement specifying the same condition' is not applied when the INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND declarative is reached as a container's USE GLOBAL; UseTierEmitter#EmitScopeTiers(globalOnly: true) omits the container's non-GLOBAL file-name cases, so the named file falls into the mode tier. adjudication.reason: A containing program holds USE GLOBAL ... ON INPUT and USE ... ON FG. A contained program with no declaratives fails to open FG, and the compiler runs the container's GLOBAL INPUT declarative. No declarative qualifies: see below. Not PB5812's question, because both USE statements are in one program.
